correctness.rationale: For odd N=2m+1>=5 the shortest-path distance matrix is circulant, and the real character of frequency two has eigenvalue F_N(s)=2 sum_{r=1}^m r^s cos(4πr/N). Recomputed geometric-sum identities F_N(0)=-1, F_N(1)=-1/[4cos²(π/N)], F_N(2)=N cos(2π/N)/[2sin²(2π/N)]. Ordered cosine coefficients have exactly one sign change for N=5,7 and exactly two (+,-,+) for N>=9. The generalized Descartes bound for exponential polynomials and signs at -infinity, 0, 1, 2 prove a unique simple root sigma_N in (1,2) and no other nonnegative roots. Differentiation at s=1 gives F'_N(1)/N²→L=[γ+log(2π)-Ci(2π)]/(8π²)>0; F''_N(s)=O(N²log²N) in 1<=s<=1+c/N². Uniform Taylor bracketing implies N²(sigma_N-1)→1/(4L)=8.0976273568665367..., with the exact C5 root log2((3+sqrt5)/2). For s>sigma_N the real mean-zero cosine eigenvector has positive distance quadratic form, disproving CND, and derivative of e^{-td^s} at t=0 is negative in this sector. Recomputed multipliers at N=5,7,9,11,31,101,301,1001 and the integral constant independently; those finite examples corroborate, not replace, the infinite proof.
